hero.h1: How to build with AI agents — and trust the result.
hero.sub: We study what makes agent-assisted engineering reliable and secure, and turn the answers into open tools and standards anyone can use.

items.p: Orchestration, decomposition and guardrails that keep AI agents on-task through long, multi-step work — without stopping early or drifting from the spec.
How agent-written code fails, how to catch it, and how to make secure-by-design the default: IAM, AppSec and authorized red-teaming of what agents produce.
What 'good' means for agent output, and how to measure it: normative playbooks, quality gates and tests that prove behavior instead of vibes.
Making the right way the easy way — tooling that installs standards, keeps them current, and gets out of the developer's way.
Findings and tools are published, not hoarded. Reproducibility is the point.
We research by building and shipping — the lab and the products feed each other.
If it isn't safe to run, it isn't done. Threat modeling and testing are part of the method.

meta.title: Principles — how we build — schematize.org
meta.desc: The engineering principles of the schematize lab: non-negotiable floors that make software written with AI agents correct, secure and maintainable — security decided server-side, tests that prove behavior, an audit trail on every change, and identity-first design.

hero.sub: AI agents can produce code fast, but speed without discipline just ships bugs faster. These are the non-negotiable floors we hold every project to — the same floors our open-source skills encode so agents follow them by default.

intro.title: Standards over vibes
intro.p: A principle only counts if a machine can check it. Each floor below maps to a concrete gate in our tooling — a test, a review rule, a required artifact — so 'done' is proven, not asserted. This is what our engineering skills install into a project, and what our research keeps sharpening.

items.h: Security is decided on the server
items.p: Authentication and authorization are enforced server-side, never in the client. Secrets never reach the browser bundle. A check in the UI is user experience — the real decision happens where the request lands, against a verified identity.

A test asserts what the software does — content, state, interaction, error and empty paths — not merely that it rendered. Coverage that doesn't fail when the behavior breaks isn't coverage. Quality gates block a merge the same way a broken build does.

items.h: Every change leaves an audit trail
items.p: No work is done until it's recorded: what changed, why, what was decided and what was rejected. The archive is part of the deliverable, not paperwork after it — so the reasoning survives the session that produced it.

Every project starts with robust IAM: identity is not an email, access is relationship-based and multi-tenant by default, and passwordless is the goal. Authorization is granular from day one, not bolted on after a breach.
Our tools are open-source and our findings are public. If it matters, you can read it, run it, fork it and build on it. Reproducibility is the point — a result you can't reproduce is an opinion.

We research by building and shipping; the lab and the products feed each other. The goal is to make the right way the easy way — tooling that installs the standard, keeps it current, and gets out of the developer's way.

cta.title: See the floors in code.
cta.p: The principles above are encoded as installable engineering skills for Claude Code — and the source is all on GitHub.
